Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- flow (Q): caudal
- velocity (v): velocidad
- head (H): carga
    DO NOT render as: a lazy anatomical calque that is NOT the language's natural hydraulic term — but an anatomically-derived word that IS the dominant local standard is correct (English 'head' is itself the body-part word repurposed); defer to the cultural standard, do not 'fix' a natural term for containing a body-part morpheme; treating it as the gauge pressure at a point. Head is energy per unit weight -- it can legitimately be READ in either height units or pressure units (the suite offers both, and defaults to psi for head loss under the US preset), so a pressure-flavoured term or a psi reading is not itself an error. The real constraint: TOTAL head (EGL, HGL) is offered in water-column units ONLY, because an EGL is an elevation and psi there is close to meaningless (Tom, 2026-07-28, encoded in the total_head unit family).; source/origin of a stream
- head loss (h_L): pérdida de carga
    DO NOT render as: calquing the English word "head" into a language whose engineers do not use a height word here. Defer to the term the language's own engineers actually use: German Druckverlust, French perte de charge, Urdu دباؤ نقصان all read literally as "pressure loss" and are all correct, dominant professional usage. NOTE ON UNITS -- this concept is legitimately read in EITHER height or pressure units, so a pressure-flavoured term is not a units error: the suite's own partial_head family (h_f, h_m, h_L) offers psi/kPa/bar/kgfcm2 and DEFAULTS to psi in the US preset. The one real constraint is on TOTAL head (EGL/HGL), which the total_head family deliberately offers in water-column units only, because an EGL is an elevation and psi there is close to meaningless (Tom, 2026-07-28) -- see the 'head' root entry.; a lazy anatomical calque that is not the local standard — an anatomically-derived word that IS the dominant standard is correct; see 'head' root entry
- friction loss (h_f): pérdida por fricción
- minor loss (h_m): pérdida localizada
- pressure (p): Presión
    DO NOT render as: the HEAD term (a height of water column) — pressure here is what a gauge reads; atmospheric or meteorological pressure senses; a stress or material-strength sense; figurative 'pressure' (urgency, coercion)
- elevation (z): Elevación
    DO NOT render as: the HEAD term — an elevation is a position above a datum, not an energy; a generic 'tall/high' adjective where the language has a surveying term; altitude in the aviation or geographic sense where a levelled survey term exists
- demand: Demanda
    DO NOT render as: economic or market demand; a legal demand/claim; a request in the everyday sense
- static head (H): Carga estática de suministro
    DO NOT render as: electrostatic / static electricity; 'stationary/motionless' in a non-hydraulic sense
- maximum allowable head (H): Presión máx. adm. tubería
    DO NOT render as: the operating / computed head (this is a fixed design limit, not the pressure the network actually develops)
- supply head (H): Carga de suministro
    DO NOT render as: an economic 'supply'; confusing supply (source) head with the delivered/residual head at a demand point
- supply curve: curva de suministro
    DO NOT render as: an economic supply curve; a demand curve
- looped network: red de tuberías mallada
    DO NOT render as: a control-flow / programming loop; a physical loop, knot, or coil
- branched network: Red de tuberías ramificada
    DO NOT render as: a literal botanical 'tree' where the language has a proper network/graph term; a looped or meshed network (branched means no loops)
- pipe line: Tramos de tubería
    DO NOT render as: a queue or line of people; a rope, cord, or cable; a line of text; a purely geometric line/segment
- pressure rating: Presión máx. adm. tubería
    DO NOT render as: a stress or material strength rather than a water pressure; blood-pressure or tyre-pressure senses; a general word for strong or high
- pressure reduction: reducción de presión
    DO NOT render as: naming a specific device (break pressure tank, BPT, pressure-reducing valve) as if the tool recommends one; depressurizing in the sense of emptying or draining the pipe
- energy grade line (EGL): línea de energía
- Manning roughness (n): coeficiente de rugosidad de Manning
- friction factor (f): factor de fricción
- draw (a diagram): dibujar
    DO NOT render as: draw water (abstract, pump, or take water from a source) -- the wrong sense here, and PLAUSIBLE in a hydraulics context, which is what makes it dangerous; pull, drag, or haul; draw as in a lottery or a tie/stalemate; withdraw money
- junction: nudo
    DO NOT render as: a road junction, crossroads, or intersection; a physical pipe fitting (tee, cross, elbow) -- a junction here is a point in the model, not a part you buy; a railway junction; an electrical junction box
- reservoir: embalse
    DO NOT render as: a TANK -- a vessel whose water level rises and falls as it fills and empties. Since ROADMAP Task 248 (2026-08-14) lpn_ models BOTH, as two separate node types, so the two must have two different words in every language. A reservoir's level is fixed and never runs down; a tank's does.; a natural lake specifically, where the language has a general storage/supply term; a reserve or reservation in the non-physical sense
- node: nodo
    DO NOT render as: a computing/server node (a transliterated loanword where the language has a real graph or network-diagram term); a knot, lump, or swelling (the anatomical/botanical sense of the Latin root); a node in the wave-physics sense (a point of zero amplitude)
- link: línea
    DO NOT render as: a hyperlink or web link -- the dominant modern sense of the English word, and the wrong one here; a chain link (the physical object); a connection in the social or logistical sense
- vertex: vértice
    DO NOT render as: a mathematical vertex of a polygon or a parabola apex, where the language has a plainer word for a bend or corner point in a drawn line; a peak or summit; a vertex in the anatomical sense (crown of the head)

    DO NOT render as: the word for a BREAK, BREAKAGE or BURST (es rotura, fr rupture, de Bruch, pt ruptura, ru razryv). - equal intervals / equal counts: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: translating 'counts' as a TALLY OF EVENTS -- it means how many elements fall in each colour band.; translating 'intervals' as intervals IN TIME.
- fire flow: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a term meaning the flow OF a fire, or a firefighting operation. This is a DESIGN REQUIREMENT, not an event.
- background image: imagen de fondo
    DO NOT render as: a backdrop in the theatrical/stage sense (the English source word was CHANGED to "background image" in Task 193 precisely to remove this transliteration lure); a wallpaper or decorative background; an online/satellite map layer -- this is a plain image file the user already has
- world file: archivo de georreferenciación
    DO NOT render as: any reading of "world" as the PLANET, the globe, or the earth. The word names a coordinate space, not a place -- "planet file", "earth file", "global file" are all wrong.; a phonetic transliteration of the English words where the language's GIS community already has a real term (fr "fichier de géoréférencement", es "archivo de georreferenciación" are the kind of thing wanted). Transliterate only where nothing established exists.; confusing it with the IMAGE file itself, or calling it a "map file" or "project file" -- it is a tiny six-line plain-text SIDECAR that travels beside the picture.; translating the file EXTENSIONS that carry it (.wld, .jgw, .tfw, .pgw). - pump curve: curva de la bomba
    DO NOT render as: a curve in the geometric/road sense; a pump characteristic confused with an efficiency or power curve -- this one is head against flow
- project (saved network): proyecto
    DO NOT render as: an engineering project or job in the contractual sense (a scheme, a works, a contract) -- this is a saved document; a projection (optical or cartographic); to project or forecast
- scenario: escenario
    DO NOT render as: a scene or setting in the dramatic/film sense; a scenario in the "worst case story" narrative sense, where the language has a modelling or variant-case term; a copy or duplicate of the network -- a scenario is a set of differences, not a second network
- zoom to extents: Ver todo
    DO NOT render as: a general "adjust/change the zoom" — this is the trap. es "Ajustar zoom" and pt "Zoom para ajustar" both shipped meaning ADJUST THE ZOOM, which describes the zoom slider, not this button. A verb meaning adjust/regulate/set is wrong unless the label also says WHAT is fitted; zoom in / zoom out / a zoom level or percentage — this command has no direction and no amount; a transliterated "zoom" loanword standing alone, where the language has a real word for showing the whole drawing; the photographic or camera sense of zoom (a lens movement)
- default (setting): predeterminado
    DO NOT render as: the financial sense — failure to pay a debt, defaulting on a loan. This is the dominant everyday sense of the English word in many languages and the single most dangerous confusion here; the legal sense — failure to appear or to act, a default judgment; a bare "reset" or "restore" with the default concept dropped entirely. ro shipped calc_defaults as just "Reseteaza" (Reset) while its own calc_defaults_confirm used "valorile implicite" correctly — the button must say WHAT is restored; a word meaning normal/usual/ordinary where the language has a real settings term. sw shipped "maadili ya kawaida" (normal values) instead of "chaguo-msingi"; "kawaida" describes what is typical, not what the software ships with; the sports sense — winning or losing by default, by forfeit
- upstream: aguas arriba
- downstream: aguas abajo
- tank: Depósito
    DO NOT render as: the word this file already uses for RESERVOIR. The page offers both tools side by side in the same toolbar, and a language that renders them with one word makes the two tools indistinguishable.; a military tank, a tracked vehicle; a fish tank or an aquarium; a fuel tank or a gas cylinder, where the language has a separate word for a WATER vessel; a transliteration of English "tank" where the language has a real word for a water storage vessel that engineers already use
- valve: Válvula
    DO NOT render as: a heart valve or any anatomical valve; a vacuum tube / electron tube (British English "valve"); a tap or faucet -- the fitting a person opens by hand at a sink, where the language distinguishes that from a pipeline valve; a transliteration of English "valve" where the language has an established pipeline term
- valve setting: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a settings/preferences sense -- this is not an option a user configures in a panel, it is the duty point the valve maintains; a placement or installation sense ("setting" a valve into a line); giving the TCV coefficient any units: it is a bare multiple of the velocity head
- override (scenario value): Valores exclusivos
    DO NOT render as: the mathematical eigenvalue sense. This is the live trap: a literal "own values" renders as es "valores propios" / pt "valores proprios" / de "Eigenwerte", which every engineer reads as EIGENVALUES. Say "values of its own" / "values set in this scenario", never the eigen- word.; an override in the authority or veto sense (overruling a person or a permission); a manual override switch on a machine; a copy or a duplicate -- an override is a single differing value, not a second network
- solver: solucionador
    DO NOT render as: the word for a physical MOTOR or ENGINE (es/pt motor, fr moteur, it motore, de Motor, ro motor, id mesin, sw injini, zh 引擎, ar محرك, he מנוע, fa موتور, uk рушій). This is the specific defect sprint 252 existed to repair.; a transliteration of English "engine" (ur انجن, bn ইঞ্জিন, my အင်ဂျင်, hi इंजन) -- same collision, plus it is a loanword where a real term exists.; reusing the word your file already uses for CALCULATOR (sw kikokotoo, am ማስያ, km ម៉ាស៊ីនគណនា). lpn.context: Hydraulic head — energy per unit weight of water, expressed as a height of water column. The ROOT concept behind head loss, velocity head, weir head, and gross/net head. A length, never a pressure. Appears as a bare label in Weir Flow (ws_headWaterHeight), Orifice (or_head), and Manning Pipe Flow (mpf_velocity_head). Acceptable English synonyms (translate the concept, not the exact word): energy elevation, hydraulic grade line (HGL).
lpn.translation_notes: Newly seeded 2026-07-20 to close the long-standing gap where only the COMPOUNDS (head loss, velocity/weir/gross/net head) had entries but the root word 'head' did not — the root is what every agent re-derived (and sometimes mistranslated as anatomical head or pressure). Values below are the roots extracted from those compound entries and are best-effort/derived, not natively verified — confirm in the term-centric sweep (see ROADMAP). Several languages split the root by sense: the hydro-power 'fall' sense uses a different word than the pipe 'head' sense (cs spád vs tlaková výška; hr/sr visina·pad vs visina; ro sarcină vs cădere; tr yük vs düşü; ar علو/الارتفاع vs الضغط). lpn.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. The English 'head' is itself jargon, and many languages express this concept in pressure terms as their professional standard — use whichever phrasing your language's hydraulic engineers actually use, and keep it consistent with the rest of that language's file.
lpn.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Five kinds are offered by what they do: a throttle valve (TCV) holding a fixed loss, a pressure reducing valve (PRV), a pressure sustaining valve (PSV) and a flow control valve (FCV). The last three open, close, or partly close by themselves as the water changes.

It must read naturally in a very narrow status strip beside the units readout, followed by a count ("Own values: 3"). Note the suite ALREADY uses "local" as a technical term -- "Minor (local) loss" -- so a rendering built on the word "local" collides with an established meaning on the same page and should be avoided. THE ENGLISH MOVED BECAUSE OF WHAT THIS SPRINT MEASURED: lpn_scenario_overrides is now 'Custom values', not 'Own values' (Tom: "I love 'custom'. 'Changed' is a little dangerous"). TEN languages independently detected and routed around the eigenvalue calque -- es pt cs it ro uk bg sr de hr -- far wider than the three Wave 0 predicted, and six hit it a second time in lpn_scenario_push_none, a key Wave 0 never flagged. 'Custom' has no calque path into mathematics in any of them, so the trap stops existing rather than being dodged 26 times. THE SECOND FINDING IS THE MORE USEFUL ONE. Clustering the renderings by MEANING split them three ways: 'its own' (13), 'custom/specific/exclusive' (7) and 'CHANGED' (cs hr bg). The third is FALSE here -- a scenario's custom value may be identical to Base's, which scenario-harness.js asserts outright -- and it was invisible in any single language. Being forced off a calque makes a translator CHOOSE a reading, so a divergence in those forced choices measures how many readings the English has. All three were corrected: cs Specificke, hr Svoje, bg Svoi, de Individuelle. ON THE hr/sr APPARENT CONTRADICTION, settled rather than split: 'vlastita vrijednost' IS a documented alternate name for eigenvalue in CROATIAN, while Serbian's dominant term uses a different root (sopstvena), so 'vlastite' is safe in sr and not in hr. Two closely related languages, two genuinely different answers -- do not harmonise them.

lpn.context: The part of a program that computes the answer. In lpn_ there are TWO of them and the UI contrasts them in one sentence: EPANET's own solver, and this suite's built-in solver. Both must be recognisable as the same KIND of thing and distinguishable from each other, so use one noun for both and let the qualifier (EPANET vs built-in) carry the difference.

The evidence that the ENGLISH was the defect, not the translations: 20+ languages were already internally inconsistent, using a correct solver word for the BUILT-IN solver and a motor word for EPANET's -- in the same sentence. sr језгро vs решавач; cs výpočetní jádro vs řešič; id mesin vs penyelesai; hi इंजन vs सॉल्वर; tr motor vs çözücü; ro motorul vs rezolvitorul. Every agent independently resolved it toward the solver word it already had. Russian had avoided the trap from the start (расчётное ядро) and Chinese noted 引擎 unambiguously means a physical engine, so there was no trade-off to make there.
